completion_data.completion_summary: Closed the Zotero write-back activation task by performing the user-gated real item-add/attach-file test against the production library (item key QWF66MNX, confirmed the .data.key envelope field, and surfaced a storage-quota block on attachment), then activating and deploying the literature extension for the first time and reconciling its README deployment-status documentation with post-deploy reality.

memory_candidates.content: zot (zotero-cli-cc) write commands (add/attach) hit the Web API directly and mutate the live server-side library, but zot's READ commands (search/read/stats, and therefore zotero-read.sh) query the local SQLite database only. A Web-API write is invisible to local reads until a running Zotero desktop client syncs it down (the item-add response's `sync_required: true` field documents this). A DOI-normalized live-library dedup check built on zotero-read.sh is therefore 'last-locally-synced', not 'current server state' -- a duplicate created moments earlier via the Web API (e.g. by a concurrent process) would not yet be visible to it.

A Zotero attach-file call that is rejected by the account's storage quota (Web API 413 'File would exceed quota') is NOT a clean no-op: Zotero's attach flow creates the child attachment item's metadata record (linkMode/filename/contentType) in a separate API call BEFORE uploading file bytes, and that record persists (md5/mtime null) even when the upload itself fails. A quota-rejected attach therefore leaves an orphaned, file-less attachment stub as a child of the target item. Confirm and clean up via a direct GET on .../items/<KEY>/children.

When activating a never-before-deployed extension in this repo's agent-system/extensions/ layout, running check-extension-docs.sh after deploy can surface Rule S (deployed file missing from index-entries.json) and Rule R (stale line_count) findings that are genuinely the activating extension's own gaps, not caused by the activation itself -- fix them in the extension's own source-store index-entries.json (never in core, and never in the deployed .claude/ tree) and redeploy to verify. Pre-existing findings in OTHER extensions (e.g. core) surfaced by the same run are a separate, usually out-of-territory concern -- check git status before assuming a FAIL was caused by your own work.
